summary: Planner C (Testing & Completion lens) on the B1–B9 + A-1 remediation. Three findings change the shape of the plan. (1) Observed: `npm run test:mutation` — a stage of `npm run verify` — is already failing before any remediation begins: four mutation rows are stale, one of them stale on committed `main` since commit add0554, three broken by the uncommitted Phase 2 session work. The harness that is supposed to prove each guarantee "has been seen to fail" is therefore not running at all, and several proposed fixes (B5 in manifests.py, B1 in refusals.py/writes.py) will edit lines that other mutation rows quote verbatim, breaking more rows. Every package must carry mutation-row maintenance in its acceptance criteria, and one package must restore the bar first. (2) Observed: B3's recommended fix contradicts an existing passing test (`engine/test_manifest.py::test_high_is_matched_on_meaning_not_spelling` asserts `coerced == ()` for "HIGH"/"high"/" High ") and a decision recorded in `memory.md`; taking B3 as written violates the contract's success criterion 6. B3 should be re-scoped to the docstring or escalated as an owner decision, not implemented. (3) Observed: B4's recommended test cannot pass today — `0005_run_store.sql:288` grants `select` on the five tables to three roles with no RLS, so a caller *can* reach them directly; the only test that can pass without a schema change is a source-shape test, and the RLS variant is a separate, riskier package. I also recommend moving B9 from fifth to first: it is the harness that judges every other package, and another session is working the repository concurrently.
information_gathered: EV-001 Observed — `backend/package.json` defines `verify` as `test && test:engine && test:doorway && test:mutation`; `test:mutation` runs `db/test/mutation-check.mjs`, `engine/mutation_check.py` and `doorway/mutation_check.py`. The mutation harnesses are a release gate, not an optional extra.

EV-002 Observed — ran the doorway harness's own preflight rule in-process against the working tree (`python -c` importing `doorway.mutation_check.MUTATIONS` and testing each `find` string against its file): four of 36 rows no longer match. Output: STALE `sessions never expire` (doorway/sessions.py), STALE `expired sessions pile up until each token is presented again` (doorway/sessions.py), STALE `removing an expired session crashes if another request removed it first` (doorway/sessions.py), STALE `the query selector is discarded before it reaches the app` (doorway/server.py).

EV-003 Observed — `backend/doorway/mutation_check.py::preflight` returns a non-empty list for those rows and `main()` prints 'STALE CHECKS — nothing was run' and returns 1. Preflight also fails a row whose named test does not exist; `test_an_entry_removed_mid_check_is_no_session_not_a_crash` is absent from `backend/doorway/test_sessions.py` (grep found only `test_expired_sessions_are_swept_when_a_new_one_is_issued`). So `npm run test:mutation` exits non-zero and nothing is evaluated.

EV-004 Observed — the server.py row was already stale on committed `main`: `git show HEAD:backend/doorway/server.py | grep -n 'selector = '` returns nothing (the line was refactored into `_query` by commit add0554 'Reject malformed query escapes'), while `git show HEAD:backend/doorway/sessions.py | grep -c _by_token` returns 10. One stale row predates the Phase 2 work; three are caused by it.

EV-005 Observed — mutation rows quote source lines that the proposed fixes will edit. `doorway/manifests.py` row 'the engine's refusal is reworded on the way out' quotes `                    "reason": reasons[0],`, which is the line B5 proposes to change. `doorway/refusals.py` rows quote `    if code == INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGE:` and `    if isinstance(error, psycopg.OperationalError):`, both inside `classify`, which B1 option 1 edits. Six `doorway/writes.py` rows quote field tuples and the `except psycopg.Error` block, which B1 option 2 and B7 touch.

EV-006 Observed — `backend/engine/test_manifest.py:112-126` (`test_high_is_matched_on_meaning_not_spelling`) asserts `checked.coerced == ()` for severities "HIGH", "high" and " High ", with the stated reason that a case variant preserves the model's meaning and recording it 'would bury the real rewrites in noise'. B3's proposed condition (`record whenever severity != risk.severity`) makes that assertion false.

EV-007 Observed — the same decision is recorded in `memory.md:1835-1852`: severity is 'matched on meaning, not spelling', and the record is for a severity that is 'genuinely unrecognisable'. `backend/engine/mutation_check.py` also has a row 'a differently-spelled High is silently downgraded to Standard' pointing at that same test, so the decision is guarded twice.

EV-008 Observed — `backend/db/migrations/0005_run_store.sql:288-295` grants `select, insert` on `cw.snapshot`, `cw.snapshot_member`, `cw.snapshot_ladder_rung`, `cw.ruleset`, `cw.ruleset_member` to three roles, and lines 265-268 enable RLS on `cw.run`, `cw.run_decision`, `cw.run_finding` only. `backend/doorway/documents.py:47-56` states the invariant and cites the same line numbers. A behavioural test of the form 'a caller cannot reach these tables' fails today by construction.

EV-009 Observed — `backend/doorway/runs.py:282-327` (`_store`) inserts into the five shared tables with `on conflict do nothing` and states 'AND NO READ-THEN-SKIP GUARD, deliberately'. Any RLS added to those tables must not disturb content-addressed sharing, which is itself guarded by a mutation row pointing at `test_runs.py::test_two_runs_against_an_unchanged_library_share_one_snapshot`.

EV-010 Observed — `backend/doorway/test_writes.py` already runs three database-free parametrized suites over `sorted(WRITES)` (lines 177, 290, 303). This is the existing, cheap vehicle for a B1 acceptance test: no `schema` fixture, no schema rebuild, no added suite minutes.

EV-011 Observed — `backend/doorway/writes.py:298` is the only `as_json=True` field in the whole write table (`Field("findings", as_json=True)`). A boundary guard that refuses dict/list for every non-`as_json` field therefore has exactly one exemption and cannot collide with anything else.

EV-012 Observed — `backend/doorway/executions.py:144-172` has its own boundary loop with `isinstance` checks already (`signatories` must be a list, each entry a dict), so B1's guard for `executions.py` has an obvious home and an obvious test file (`test_executions.py`).

EV-013 Observed — `backend/doorway/conftest.py` rebuilds the schema per test via `prepare()`, and `backend/doorway/setup.py:31-45` runs `alter role cw_app login password …` on every call and then *verifies* NOINHERIT with a select rather than rewriting it. `backend/db/migrations/0016_doorway_login.sql:33-47` runs `alter role cw_app noinherit` in the else branch and then `grant cw_viewer, … to cw_app` unconditionally — a third cluster-wide role write per rebuild that the bug report does not name.

EV-014 Observed — `backend/doorway/mutation_check.py`'s own docstring and `main()` record that six concurrent rebuilds collided with `tuple concurrently updated` (five of six failed) and that nine of twenty-four lanes died in their fixture on one run. B9 is not only a nuisance in `pytest`; it is the reason the mutation harness needs a serial retry pass, and it silently degrades the evidence the whole remediation will be judged by.

EV-015 Observed — `backend/doorway/test_prohibitions.py` already owns the role-boundary tests and takes both `db` and `owner_url` fixtures (lines 19-45), including `test_sign_in_reads_as_the_least_privileged_role`. That is the natural home for the A-1/D-1 boundary test, and it needs no new fixture machinery.

EV-016 Observed — `CLAUDE.md` forbids testing wording ('a test checks what the system does, never the words'), and `audit_results.md` section D-1 already specifies the A-1 test in behavioural terms. Every acceptance criterion below is written as a status code, a row count, a raised exception type or a process exit code — never a message string.

EV-017 Observed — `bug_report.md` header: doorway suite is 566 tests in 13m37s with a per-test schema rebuild; engine is 202 tests. Any acceptance test that needs the `schema` fixture costs roughly a second of rebuild plus its own time, so DB-free unit tests are strongly preferred where the guarantee allows.
diagnosis: Observed — The remediation's own scoreboard is broken before it starts. `npm run test:mutation` aborts in preflight with four stale rows (EV-002, EV-003), so the repository's stated standard — 'a passing suite is not the same as those guarantees having been SEEN TO FAIL' — is currently unmet for all 36 doorway guarantees, not just the four. Any package that reports 'verify is green' without fixing this is reporting on a stage that never ran.

Observed — This is the same failure mode `audit_results.md` C-2 names (two guard tests committed red), arriving in a second harness. Commit add0554 changed `server.py` and left the mutation row quoting a line that no longer exists (EV-004). A guard that cannot match is not a guard, and the harness says so in its own preflight docstring.

Inferred (from EV-005) — Fixes and mutation rows are coupled by verbatim source text. B5 edits the exact line a manifests.py row quotes; B1 edits lines two refusals.py rows and several writes.py rows quote. If mutation-row maintenance is not part of each package's definition of done, the remediation will land, `pytest` will be green, and `test:mutation` will still be red — with more rows stale than today.

Observed — B3 is not a defect with an agreed fix; it is a contested decision. The behaviour the bug report calls a broken promise is asserted by a passing test (EV-006) and recorded as a deliberate choice in `memory.md` (EV-007). Success criterion 6 of the Objective Contract forbids a package that needs a passing test weakened. The genuine defect is the docstring's phrase 'every real rewrite', which does not distinguish a change of spelling from a change of meaning.

Observed — B4's recommended acceptance test is unachievable as stated. The five tables carry select grants and no RLS (EV-008), so 'a caller cannot reach it' is false today at the database level; the invariant that actually holds is 'no code path lets a caller-supplied id reach them first', which is a property of the source, not of the database. Two different packages hide inside B4's one sentence.

Inferred (from EV-008, EV-009) — The stronger B4 fix (RLS scoped through `cw.run`) is a schema change with real blast radius: content-addressed sharing, the `cw.run_snapshot`/`run_contract`/`run_summary` views (which run with the view owner's rights unless `security_invoker` is set) and the rebuild path in `documents.py` all read those tables. It must not be bundled with the cheap invariant test.

Observed — B9 is a prerequisite, not a tidy-up. The harness collision degrades both `pytest` (one error in 566) and the mutation harness (nine of twenty-four lanes never evaluated, EV-014), and the Objective Contract's assumption A5 says another session is working this repository concurrently. Ranked fifth, as `bug_report.md` proposes, every earlier package is validated by an instrument known to be unreliable.

Inferred (from EV-013) — The B9 fix as recommended ('wrap the alter role in setup.py and the DO block in 0016 in a retry') is narrower than the collision surface: `grant … to cw_app` at 0016:45 is a third unconditional cluster-wide role write per rebuild. The 'verify rather than rewrite' alternative the bug report prefers removes the write entirely for `noinherit`, but cannot for the password (a password cannot be read back), so this needs an explicit decision rather than an implicit one.

Observed — A-1 and D-1 are one package, not two. `audit_results.md` says plainly there is no test today and the probe shape is known; `test_prohibitions.py` already has the fixtures (EV-015). Shipping the migration without the test recreates precisely the condition that let A-1 land.

Inferred (from EV-010, EV-011, EV-017) — B1's acceptance belongs at two levels: a database-free parametrized test over `sorted(WRITES)` proving `Write.bind` refuses a dict/list in any non-`as_json` field (cheap, total coverage of the write table), plus one end-to-end test per non-`Write.bind` binding site (`executions.py`, `runs.py`) proving the status code is 400. Testing it only end-to-end would multiply the 13-minute suite; testing it only at unit level would miss the two sites the bug report names.
symptoms: Observed — `python doorway/mutation_check.py` prints 'STALE CHECKS — nothing was run, because these prove nothing' and exits 1, so `npm run verify` fails at its last stage regardless of the product's state (EV-002, EV-003).

Observed — Three of the four stale rows name guarantees about sessions that no longer have any mutation coverage at all: sessions never expiring, expired rows piling up, and a row removed mid-check crashing. The Phase 2 store replaced the implementation and no replacement guarantees were written (EV-002).
Observed — One mutation row names a test that no longer exists (`test_an_entry_removed_mid_check_is_no_session_not_a_crash`), which the harness's preflight treats as fatal (EV-003).

Observed — `bug_report.md` records one error in 566 doorway tests, surfacing as `tuple concurrently updated` inside `alter role cw_app noinherit` during an unrelated read test, and the suite passes in isolation (165 passed).
Observed — `audit_results.md` D-1: no test asserts who may reach `cw.session`; A-1 was found by reading and confirmed by a throwaway probe.

Observed — `audit_results.md` D-2: a concurrency test's iteration count was cut from 200 to 50 with no note, and its docstring was generalised away from the two failures it existed to catch — a guard quietly made a quarter as likely to fire.
Observed — `audit_results.md` C-2: two guard tests were committed to `main` in a failing state, one of them failing on the very guarantee it exists to protect.
consequences: Inferred (EV-001, EV-003) — Until the mutation bar is restored, no package in this remediation can produce trustworthy completion evidence: 'verify is green' is currently unobtainable, and 'the suite passes' is a weaker claim than this repository has chosen to accept.

Inferred (EV-005) — Fixing B1 and B5 without touching `mutation_check.py` converts three or more further rows from live to stale, so the remediation would leave the bar worse than it found it while every individual package reported success.

Observed/Inferred (EV-006, EV-007) — Implementing B3 as written would require editing or deleting `test_high_is_matched_on_meaning_not_spelling` and would silently reverse a decision recorded in `memory.md`, breaching contract constraint 6 and the house rule that a guarantee leaves the suite with a reason or not at all.

Inferred (EV-008) — Writing B4's acceptance test as a behavioural database test produces a package that cannot pass, which either stalls the plan or pressures the implementer into a schema change that was never scoped.

Inferred (EV-014, contract assumption A5) — With B9 unfixed and a second session active, any package's validation run can fail in a fixture with a message about role inheritance. The likely reaction — rerun until green — is exactly how a real failure gets normalised as flakiness.
Inferred (EV-015, audit D-1) — A-1 fixed without its boundary test leaves the next migration free to reopen the grant, and nothing in the suite would notice; the audit says so explicitly.
proposed_actions: Package WP-T0 (first, blocking) — Restore the mutation bar before any product change. Re-point the four stale rows (EV-002): three sessions.py rows must be rewritten as guarantees of the database-backed store (a session past its expiry is not honoured; expired rows are swept; a row deleted concurrently is not a crash), each naming a test that exists in the current `test_sessions.py`/`test_retirement.py`; the server.py selector row must be re-pointed at the current `_query` implementation. Acceptance: `python doorway/mutation_check.py` completes preflight and reports every row `ok`. Owner: one, file `backend/doorway/mutation_check.py` plus any test it must name.

Package WP-B9 (second) — Stop the cluster-wide role writes colliding. Decide explicitly between (a) retry-once on `tuple concurrently updated` around the role statements in `setup.py` and `0016`, and (b) 'verify rather than rewrite' — the model `setup.py:44-52` already uses for NOINHERIT — extending the check to `rolcanlogin` and the six role memberships, leaving only the password write. Scope must include `grant … to cw_app` at `0016:45`, which the bug report does not name (EV-013). Acceptance: a reproduction test that runs N concurrent `prepare()` calls against one cluster and asserts no `InternalError`, run before and after the fix.

Package WP-B1 (third) — Refuse a dict or list at the boundary in `Write.bind` for every field not declared `as_json=True`, and add the equivalent guard to the two sites that bind outside it (`executions.py`, `runs.py`). Whether `refusals.classify` is widened as well is a separate decision: the two are not exclusive, but a `ProgrammingError` with `sqlstate = None` is a driver refusal and classifying it as 500 is independently wrong. Acceptance: a database-free parametrized test over `sorted(WRITES)` (EV-010) plus one 400-status end-to-end test per non-`Write.bind` site, plus a new mutation row for the guard.

Package WP-A1 (fourth, approval-sensitive) — The A-1 migration and its boundary test ship together as one package (audit D-1). The test belongs in `test_prohibitions.py` (EV-015): seed an ordinary `viewer` account, sign an administrator in, then select from `cw.session` as that viewer and assert zero rows, and assert the delete affects zero rows. Add a mutation row that breaks the new policy or grant and requires that test to fail. The choice between a dedicated lookup role and the actor-scoped policy, and between editing `0032` and adding `0033`, is the owner's.

Package WP-B2 (fifth) — Split the transaction around the model call. Acceptance is the audit's own probe, promoted to a permanent test: stub the model call, and from an independent connection (the `owner_url` fixture already provides one) assert zero `idle in transaction` backends belonging to the serving pool while the model call is running. Add a mutation row that puts the call back inside the transaction and requires that test to fail.

Package WP-B4a (sixth, cheap) — Pin the invariant `documents.py` currently states in prose as a source-shape test: no module composes a caller-supplied identifier into a statement against `cw.snapshot`, `cw.snapshot_member`, `cw.snapshot_ladder_rung`, `cw.ruleset` or `cw.ruleset_member` without first resolving through `cw.run`. This is achievable today; the behavioural version is not (EV-008).

Package WP-B4b (deferred, separate) — If RLS on the five tables is wanted, scope it as its own package with its own risk budget: policies scoped through `cw.run`, an explicit decision on `security_invoker` for the three run views, and regression coverage for content-addressed sharing (EV-009). Do not bundle it with WP-B4a.

Package WP-B567 (seventh, batch) — B5: guard `reasons[0]` in `runs.py` and `manifests.py` and pin the coupling with a test that asserts a 409 with a non-empty reason for a manifest whose category is unknown; the mutation row quoting `"reason": reasons[0],` must be re-pointed in the same package (EV-005). B6: bind the audit event as a parameter at all six call sites, with a source-shape test asserting no f-string interpolation in a `cw.audit(` call. B7: `demanded = spec.required or (…)`, with a unit test on `Field`/`Write.bind` covering the combination that has no live use.

Package WP-B8 (eighth, documentation and hygiene) — Correct the stale comment in `app.py`, remove the unused `threading` import and add the missing `Database` import in `sessions.py`. Acceptance is a type-checker or import-time check, not a test; and per `CLAUDE.md` the rationale record for the session clock change belongs in `memory.md`.

Escalation, not a package — B3 must go back to the owner as a decision. The behaviour the bug report calls broken is asserted by a passing engine test and recorded as deliberate in `memory.md` (EV-006, EV-007). Recommended resolution: amend the `check_manifest` docstring so 'every real rewrite' says what the code and the test already agree on — a rewrite of meaning is recorded, a rewrite of spelling is not — and close B3 as documentation. If the owner instead wants spelling changes recorded, that is a new decision, a new memory record, and an edit to a currently-passing test, and it must be scoped as such.

Cross-cutting rule for every package — Definition of done is: the named tests pass; `python doorway/mutation_check.py` and `python engine/mutation_check.py` both exit 0; each new guarantee has a mutation row that has been seen to fail; and the decision and its rationale are recorded in `memory.md` per `CLAUDE.md`. No acceptance criterion asserts message text.

Cheap recurrence guard (recommended, small) — Run the mutation harnesses' preflight (a pure text check that takes seconds) early in `npm run verify`, before the 13-minute suites, so a stale row is reported in seconds rather than surviving on `main` for several commits as this one did (EV-004).

risks: Observed — Implementing B3 as recommended breaks a passing test and reverses a recorded decision (EV-006, EV-007). Highest-consequence risk in the set because it looks like a one-line fix.

Inferred (EV-005) — Silent mutation-row breakage: a package passes its own tests, the harness goes stale, and the failure surfaces later as an unrelated red bar that the next session may 'fix' by deleting the row.

Inferred (EV-008, EV-009) — Adding RLS to the five shared tables can break content-addressed sharing or the three run views, both of which are themselves guarded by mutation rows; a partial fix here trades a latent exposure for a live regression.
Inferred (EV-014, contract A5) — Validation runs during this remediation may fail in fixtures for harness reasons, and the flakiness is indistinguishable from a real defect unless B9 lands first.
Inferred (EV-013) — A B9 retry-only fix leaves the `grant … to cw_app` write unretried; the collision would become rarer and therefore harder to attribute.
Inferred (EV-017) — Acceptance tests written at the endpoint level where a unit test would do add real minutes to a 13-minute suite that is already run by `npm run verify` on every machine.

Inferred (CLAUDE.md, audit C-2) — Message-text assertions are the repository's most repeated self-inflicted failure. B1, B5 and A-1 all produce tempting message assertions; every criterion must be a status code, a row count or an exception type.

assumptions: Assumed — I did not execute `pytest` or `npm run verify`; no PostgreSQL was started in this read-only pass. The mutation-bar failure is established from the harness's own preflight rule, which I evaluated in-process against the real sources (EV-002), not from running the harness end to end. The stale-row finding is therefore Observed; the claim that the rest of the suite currently passes is taken from `bug_report.md`.
Assumed — The four stale rows are the complete set at the moment of this pass; a concurrent session committing to `main` (contract assumption A5) may add or remove rows.

Inferred — Views (`cw.run_snapshot`, `cw.run_contract`, `cw.run_summary`) execute with the view owner's rights unless `security_invoker` is set; I read the migration text but did not query `pg_class` to confirm the option. This matters only for WP-B4b.
Assumed — 'Work packages' is the stopping point, so no test file is written in this run; every acceptance criterion above is specified to be executable, not executed.

Assumed — The three replacement session mutation rows can be written against tests that already exist in `test_sessions.py`/`test_retirement.py`; if not, WP-T0 also writes those tests, which is why it is sized as a package rather than an edit.
unresolved_questions: Does the owner want case-variant severities recorded in `coerced` (reversing the decision at `memory.md:1835-1852` and editing a passing test), or is B3 closed as a docstring correction? Nothing downstream can size B3 until this is answered.
